tactical.rationale: At tactical weights the two factors that matter most are Policy and Rates at 0.24 and Inflation and Growth at 0.18, and they point in different directions with different intensities. Policy is Neutral because sterling's 3.75% Bank Rate is the third highest in the G10+SGD set and delivers a 150bp premium over the ECB, a 275bp premium over the Bank of Japan and a 375bp premium over the SNB, yet only 12.5bp over the Fed - and the Cable forward curve at minus 12 pips over twelve months proves the market agrees there is no carry in the primary pair [2][7]. Inflation and Growth is Bullish because the July flash composite PMI jumped to 52.1 from 49.3 with services at 51.8 against a 49.4 consensus, GfK consumer confidence rose six points to minus 17 in its largest monthly gain since November 2023, and the Bank's own projection has headline CPI RISING toward a 3.2% Q4 peak, which keeps the 87.2% December hike probability alive through August [8][35][36]. The weighted result of +0.1012 is a weak Bullish, and the honest reading is that sterling has already banked most of this: Cable is up 1.56% on the month and sits 0.63% above a converged 200-day moving average at 1.33993. The factors reinforce in one place and conflict in another. USD Liquidity at Bullish 57 reinforces the growth story, because a Federal Reserve that has ended quantitative tightening and bought roughly USD 30.4bn of Treasury bills in July is easing the global funding backdrop for every non-dollar currency [22][40]. Flows conflict directly: leveraged funds are net long 41,097 contracts at the 88th percentile after adding for four consecutive weeks, and that is the marginal position most exposed to a disappointment [15]. What is priced is the vote and not the press conference - an 87.2% cumulative December hike probability - a single-vendor figure, flagged - against a Bank survey median of no change over the year ahead and a July Monetary Policy Report central projection that undershoots the 2% target at the policy horizon [8][10][11]. Our tactical edge is that this gap will not close inside the window, because there is no MPC communication before 17 September and headline CPI is rising for mechanical energy reasons - so the hawkish premium persists even though we believe it is wrong. The path of least resistance is therefore a grind higher into the 1.3500-1.3557 option and range resistance, with the July high at 1.35573 the obvious magnet given a USD 388mn expiry at 1.3500 was already breached on 31 July [17]. The dated catalysts are dense and clustered: Q2 GDP and June monthly GDP on 13 August, the labour market report with the average-weekly-earnings seasonal-adjustment review on 18 August, July CPI on 19 August, and the August flash PMI with July public finances on 21 August. Conviction drivers are the freshness and size of the July activity surprise, the mechanical rise in headline CPI, and a dollar-liquidity impulse that is unusually clear; what stops this being more than a coin flip in the other direction is precisely that all three are observable and none depends on forecasting. Actionability is moderate: the trade is a 90-pip grind with a well-defined 1.3400 stop at the moving-average convergence, which is a 0.7:1 base-case ratio that only becomes attractive when the 25% upside case at 1.3700 is included, taking the probability-weighted ratio to roughly 3:1.

g10_ranking.commentary: Sterling ranks fifth of eleven tactically. It beats the dollar on a flat broad index and an easing Fed balance sheet, the euro on a 150bp carry advantage and a 183bp gilt-Bund spread, the Canadian dollar on 150bp of carry against a central bank with CPI-trim at 1.8%, the franc on 375bp of carry against a zero policy rate, and the krona on 200bp of carry. It loses to the krone and the Australian dollar, which out-carry it and are the direct beneficiaries of the same commodity shock that taxes the UK terms of trade; to the yen, which has just seen suspected coordinated intervention and sits at an all-time real-effective low; to the Singapore dollar, which combines 5.7% year-on-year growth with an appreciating MAS band; and to the kiwi, whose central bank is actively hiking with CPI at 4.1%. The ranking captures the essential problem: sterling's carry is good against currencies nobody wants to be short and poor against the ones that are actually moving.

strategic.rationale: At strategic weights the framework re-ranks the evidence decisively: External Balance rises from 0.06 to 0.16, Guidance from 0.07 to 0.12 and Fiscal from 0.04 to 0.07, while Inflation and Growth falls from 0.18 to 0.10 and Risk Appetite from 0.10 to 0.05. Policy and Rates stays at 0.24 and it flips from Neutral to Bearish, which alone accounts for minus 0.1392 of the minus 0.3500 net. The mechanism is that every relative rate leg moves against sterling over one to six months: the ECB is 77-83% priced to hike on 10 September with euro-area core HICP at 2.5% against UK core at 2.6%, the Fed held 9-3 with three dissents to HIKE and core PCE at 3.29%, the RBNZ is already hiking with CPI at 4.1%, Norges Bank has published a path above 4.5%, and the Bank of Japan is normalising [22][23][24][25][26]. Sterling is the only major currency whose central bank has both the weakest inflation case to tighten and the most tightening already priced, at 87.2% cumulative by December [8]. External Balance at Bearish 72 is the second pillar and it is the most underpriced element in the whole dossier: a 2.84%-of-GDP current-account deficit with a 7.6%-of-GDP goods deficit meets a 47.1% energy import dependency and an NBP gas price up 64.95% year-on-year, and Cable rose 1.56% in the month that gas rose 40.86% [4][20][32]. The factors reinforce rather than conflict, which is why the score is decisive: a deteriorating external balance requires foreign capital, foreign capital requires a yield premium, and the yield premium is exactly what we expect the Bank of England to remove at the 5 November Monetary Policy Report - which is also eight days after the 28 October Budget delivers the cycle's only formal fiscal-rules assessment on a headroom number computed before Brent hit USD 117 [6][11]. What is priced is a hawkish Bank of England, a resolved political situation and no terms-of-trade cost; what we expect is a Bank of England that repeats a below-target medium-term projection, a Budget that tests a new government's fiscal discipline against a 10% probability of winning a majority, and an energy import bill that compounds monthly [9][11]. The path of least resistance is lower, expressed most cleanly through EUR/GBP rather than Cable, because EUR/GBP strips out the dollar leg and captures both sides of the convergence trade at a twenty-day realised volatility of just 3.56%. The dated catalysts are 10 September for the ECB, 17 September for the MPC and the annual quantitative-tightening review, 28 October for the Budget and OBR forecast, and 5 November for the Monetary Policy Report. The conviction drivers are that four of the five bearish factors rest on published data rather than forecasts, and that the single most important piece of evidence - the July MPR's own 1.7% CPI projection for 2028 Q1 on a tightening conditioning path - is the Bank of England telling the market it is wrong, in the Bank's own framework [11]. Actionability is high: a 283-pip base-case move with a 167-pip upside-case stop gives a 1.7:1 base ratio and a 7.8:1 probability-weighted ratio, and the expression can be bought as convexity rather than held as spot because the volatility term structure carries no Budget premium at all.

g10_ranking.commentary: Sterling ranks ninth of eleven strategically, a four-place fall from its tactical rank, and the fall is driven almost entirely by the re-weighting of External Balance from 0.06 to 0.16. It beats only the Canadian dollar, which faces minus 0.05% year-on-year GDP, CPI-trim at 1.8% and a central bank with no tightening impulse, and the krona, whose 1.75% policy rate and 0.4% CPIF ex-energy give it no carry defence. It loses to everything else: to the krone and the Australian dollar on carry and commodity terms of trade, to the Singapore dollar on 5.7% growth and a 16.7% current-account surplus, to the franc and the yen on surplus-driven structural support, to the kiwi on an actively hiking central bank, to the euro on a September hike and a 1.7% surplus, and to the dollar on a 3.29% core PCE that gives the Fed the stronger tightening case. The uncomfortable summary is that sterling's principal claim - high carry - is the one attribute the strategic window is most likely to erode.

consensus_divergence.consensus_view: The eleven-institution consensus published on 15 July 2026 has GBP/USD trending gradually higher through to early 2027, with near-term consolidation before firmer gains emerge in the new year, and notes that more than ten cents separates the most bullish from the most bearish call for end-2026 - one of the widest dispersions in the G10 forecast set. Lloyds expects range trade propped around 1.3200 with a return above 1.3600 requiring credible macroeconomic policy steps, and caps sterling against the euro at the post-Brexit EUR/GBP 0.8200 support shelf. The market forward curve is flatter than the analyst consensus: GBP/USD twelve-month forwards imply 1.34714, essentially unchanged, while the OIS strip prices an 87.2% cumulative Bank Rate increase by December [2][8].
consensus_divergence.our_view: We agree with the near-term consolidation and disagree with the firmer gains in the new year, because the new year sits on the far side of both the 28 October Budget and the front-end repricing we expect at the 5 November Monetary Policy Report. We are tactically Bullish to 1.3575 over two to four weeks and strategically Bearish to 1.3200 by end-January 2027, with EUR/GBP rising to 0.8750. We think the 87.2% December hike probability is roughly 30 percentage points too high and that fair value is nearer 50-55%.
consensus_divergence.divergence_magnitude: Roughly 270-450 pips against the consensus direction at the six-month point, and about 285 pips against the twelve-month forward outright of 1.34714. On EUR/GBP the divergence is larger in relative terms: consensus and Lloyds both see the cross grinding toward 0.8200-0.8400, we see 0.8750, a gap of 350-550 pips.
consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: Four reasons, in order of importance. First, the market underweights the July Monetary Policy Report's own arithmetic: a central projection of CPI at 1.7% in 2028 Q1 and 1.9% in 2029 Q3, conditioned on a market curve embedding roughly two hikes by Q3 2027, is the Bank of England formally stating that market pricing is too restrictive - the identical signal, inverted, that justified the 2024 cuts [11]. Second, the market has priced the 6-3 vote and discounted the Governor's published opening remarks, which attribute the curve's upward slope to 'risk premia rather than expectations of future levels of Bank Rate' and disclose that the Bank's own Market Participants Survey median expects no change over the year ahead [10]. Third, consensus systematically underweights Factor 5 at its 0.16 strategic weight: a 2.84%-of-GDP current-account deficit with a 7.6%-of-GDP goods deficit and 47.1% energy import dependency, meeting an NBP gas price up 64.95% year-on-year, is a compounding drain that no bank forecast in the sample explicitly models [4][20][32]. Fourth, consensus is anchored on an OBR headroom figure of GBP 23.6bn computed in March 2026, before the escalation that took Brent to USD 117, and the fiscal rules are now assessed only once a year - so the entire cycle's verdict lands in a single release on 28 October [6].

If the front end reprices as we expect, roughly 25bp of removed hike premium is historically worth 1.5-2.0% on the sterling effective exchange rate, which maps to the 1.3200 target almost exactly.
consensus_divergence.risk_if_wrong: If consensus is right and the Bank of England hikes while the Budget passes cleanly, the 140,911-contract asset-manager short covers into a rally and Cable reaches 1.3650-1.3800, costing 167-317 pips on a spot short. The specific mechanism that would hurt most is a hike delivered on 17 September alongside a QT slowdown that eases the long end simultaneously - a hawkish rate move without the fiscal offset - which is why we prefer defined-risk convexity to open-ended spot.

It carries the widest rate differential in the set at 375bp against an SNB pinned at 0.00% with an explicit stated willingness to intervene against franc strength, which caps the downside from the other leg [29]. The carry-to-vol ratio of 0.59 is the best available and thirty days of carry is worth 33.6 pips of cushion against 1.4 pips in Cable. Valuation is silent: at 1.08918 against a real-effective implied fair value of 1.08613, sterling is 0.28% rich versus the franc, so nothing opposes the carry.

cleanest_bearish_expression.rationale: For the strategic Bearish leg, long EUR/GBP is decisively the cleanest expression. It strips out the dollar entirely, so the trade is a pure statement about UK versus euro-area fundamentals rather than a bet on the Fed. It captures both sides of the convergence: an ECB 77-83% priced to hike on 10 September and a Bank of England we expect to be repriced dovishly at the 5 November MPR, which compresses the 150bp policy gap from both ends [8][24]. Twenty-day realised volatility of 3.56% is the lowest of any sterling expression, so the same conviction can be held at larger size, and the gilt-Bund spread at 183bp - the widest since September 2022 - is a mean-reversion tailwind. Spot 0.85539, target 0.8750. The honest cost is carry: sterling's 150bp premium means a long EUR/GBP forward position pays away roughly 64 pips over six months, about a third of the 196-pip target, which argues for expressing it as bought convexity into the 28 October Budget rather than as a held forward.

relative_value_pairs.thesis: A durable 150bp carry pickup against the one central bank in the set with no tightening impulse whatsoever - CPI-trim at 1.8%, CPI-median at 1.9%, unemployment at 6.5% and GDP contracting 0.05% year-on-year. The gilt-Canada 10Y spread of 145bp almost exactly matches the policy gap, so there is no adverse term premium; the offset is that sterling is 3.04% rich versus the Canadian dollar on relative real-effective deviation.

The purest energy-shock relative-value pair. Norway runs a 15.59%-of-GDP current-account surplus against the UK's 2.84% deficit, Norges Bank has published a path above 4.5% by end-2026 and already out-carries sterling by 50bp, and the same gas and oil move that taxes the UK terms of trade funds the Norwegian one [30]. The counter-argument is valuation: sterling is 5.32% cheap versus the krone on relative real-effective deviation, so this is a fundamentals-over-valuation trade and should be sized accordingly.

The one place sterling has a genuine valuation cushion: it is 6.22% cheap versus the Australian dollar, whose real effective rate is 6.42% above its own 30-month mean after a 9.81% real appreciation. The trade pays away 60bp of carry, so it is a tactical mean-reversion expression rather than a strategic holding, and it should be closed if the RBA hikes on 11 August.

cross_horizon_consistency.summary: The horizons diverge sharply: tactically Bullish at conviction 2 with a net score of +0.1012, strategically Bearish at conviction 3 with a net score of minus 0.3500 - a swing of 0.46 across the same ten factors.
cross_horizon_consistency.divergence_explanation: The divergence is mechanical and comes from three sources. First, five factors change stance between horizons - Policy and Rates from Neutral to Bearish, Inflation and Growth from Bullish to Bearish, Risk Appetite from Bullish to Neutral, Flows from Bearish to Bullish, Guidance from Neutral to Bearish and Fiscal from Neutral to Bearish - and each change has a specific, dated mechanism rather than a change of mood. Second, the weights themselves re-rank: External Balance rises from 0.06 to 0.16, Guidance from 0.07 to 0.12 and Fiscal from 0.04 to 0.07, while Inflation and Growth falls from 0.18 to 0.10, so the framework deliberately promotes the structural factors that all point one way. Third, the calendar does the rest: the tactical window contains only data releases through 21 August, while the strategic window contains the ECB on 10 September, the MPC and quantitative-tightening review on 17 September, the Budget and OBR forecast on 28 October and the Monetary Policy Report on 5 November.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: Mid-to-late October. The specific pivot is the 28 October Budget, with the 5 November Monetary Policy Report eight days later as confirmation. Before that date headline CPI is still rising toward the Bank's projected 3.2% Q4 peak and the hawkish premium has no reason to decay; after it, both the fiscal and the monetary uncertainty resolve simultaneously. A secondary, earlier inflection is 10 September, when an ECB hike would begin compressing the 150bp differential and turn EUR/GBP before Cable.
cross_horizon_consistency.catalyst_for_transition: The 28 October Budget is the primary catalyst because it carries the cycle's only formal fiscal-rules assessment, on an OBR headroom figure of GBP 23.6bn computed before Brent hit USD 117, delivered by a Chancellor eight days into a new government that has already announced four loosening measures [6]. The confirming catalyst is the 5 November Monetary Policy Report, where the Committee must either validate an 87.2% December hike probability or repeat a below-target medium-term projection [8][11].
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Run the tactical long and the strategic short as separate books with separate risk, not as a single netted position. The tactical expression is spot GBP/CHF or Cable with a hard stop at the 1.3400 moving-average convergence and a horizon that ends with the 21 August flash PMI. The strategic expression is long EUR/GBP, or October-November convexity bought while the volatility term structure carries no Budget premium, initiated on strength into the 1.3550-1.3650 region rather than at spot. The two are not contradictory: they are the same view about a hawkish premium that persists for six more weeks and then decays.

Independent vendor references for the same session printed 1.34820 and 1.3483 on a New York close basis and 1.3421 on the ECB 16:00 CET fixing; the New York-close references agree to within 1.5 pips and the fixing difference reflects a post-fix rally, so 1.34834 is well corroborated. Sterling ERI 106.39 at 14 July 2026, the last published daily value (flagged - no end-July reading is published on the cited page); BIS real broad REER 111.41 for June 2026.

The Cable one-month forward is exactly flat, which is the mechanical consequence of a 12.5bp policy differential.

3m.annualised_pct: +0.03% (positive = sterling appreciating in the forwards). Rebased from the 24 July three-month outright of 1.3316 against a 1.3315 spot [2]. A one-pip premium over three months is indistinguishable from zero.

6m.annualised_pct: -0.01%. Rebased from the 24 July six-month outright of 1.3314 [2]. For reference the twelve-month point is minus 12 pips, an outright of 1.34714 and an annualised discount of 0.09%, which is broadly consistent with the 12.5bp Bank Rate premium over Fed funds and implies a cross-currency basis close to flat.

edge.1m: +92 pips of sterling upside (forward implies 1.34834, we expect 1.3575). This is the tactical grind-higher thesis and it is the only positive edge in the decomposition.
edge.3m: -134 pips of sterling downside (forward implies 1.34844, we expect 1.3350). The three-month point straddles the 28 October Budget and captures the first leg of the repricing.
edge.6m: -282 pips of sterling downside (forward implies 1.34824, we expect 1.3200). This is the strategic short and the largest edge in the dossier. Selling the six-month forward at 1.34824 is the mechanically efficient expression.

forward_vs_spot.interpretation: The defining feature of the Cable forward curve is that it is flat - 0.0 pips at one month, plus 1 at three, minus 1 at six and minus 12 at twelve - because sterling's 12.5bp advantage over the Fed funds midpoint is too small to generate meaningful points [2]. That has two consequences. First, the entire expected return in Cable is spot: there is no carry to earn on a long and none to pay on a short, which makes a strategic short costless to hold, an unusual property for a currency whose policy rate sits above the dollar's. Second, the flat curve means the market is NOT pricing the convergence we expect - if the front end repriced by the 25bp we anticipate, the six-month forward would move to roughly 1.3400 by construction, so the forward curve currently embeds no part of our thesis and the full 282-pip six-month edge is available. By contrast the EUR/GBP forward curve does carry a real differential and it runs AGAINST the long EUR/GBP expression: the twelve-month EUR/GBP forward implies roughly 0.8687 against a spot of 0.85539, a 133-pip sterling forward discount reflecting the 150bp policy gap, so buying EUR/GBP forward means paying up. Over the six-month strategic horizon that negative carry costs roughly 64 pips against a 196-pip base-case target, consuming about a third of it. That is a genuine and material cost, and it is the second reason - alongside the squeeze risk in the 140,911-contract asset-manager short - that we prefer to express the strategic view as bought convexity into the late-October window rather than as a held forward position.

key_catalysts.event: Reserve Bank of Australia policy decision and Statement on Monetary Policy
key_catalysts.rationale: The RBA holds the only policy rate above sterling's at 4.35% and has already delivered 75bp of hikes in 2026 with trimmed-mean inflation stuck at 3.6%. A hike would widen the 60bp gap against sterling and remove the tactical GBP/AUD mean-reversion case, which currently rests on sterling being 6.22% cheap on relative real-effective deviation.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - a hold is the base case with an explicit tightening bias retained in the statement
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: GBP/AUD primarily; GBP/NZD secondarily through Antipodean correlation

key_catalysts.event: ONS Q2 2026 first quarterly GDP estimate, June monthly GDP and UK trade (June)
key_catalysts.rationale: The first hard read on how badly the Q2 energy shock hit UK output, released simultaneously with the June trade data that will show the goods deficit under NBP gas at 143 pence per therm. Services PMI was in contraction at 48.8 in June, so Q2 GDP is at risk, but Q1 came in at +0.6% quarter-on-quarter and the three-month-on-three-month monthly rate was +0.7% to May.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - no consensus was retrievable for the Q2 print and the market is anchored on the July PMI rebound rather than the Q2 outturn

key_catalysts.rationale: Norges Bank has published a rate path just above 4.5% for end-2026 and already out-carries sterling by 50bp while running a 15.59%-of-GDP current-account surplus funded by the same energy shock that taxes the UK. A hike widens the differential and confirms the energy-exporter versus energy-importer divergence.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - a hike at either the 13 August or 24 September meeting is the published path, with timing uncertain
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: GBP/NOK; also relevant to the sterling ERI given Norway's trade weight

key_catalysts.event: ONS labour market overview including Average Weekly Earnings, with the AWE seasonal-adjustment review
key_catalysts.rationale: The highest-variance UK release of the tactical window. Private-sector regular pay at 2.9% is the single most dovish datapoint in the UK picture, and ONS has stated the AWE seasonal-adjustment review 'may lead to revisions to the entire historical average weekly earnings time series and will be implemented in our August 2026 publication'. A revision either way resets the wage-persistence debate that underpins the 87.2% December hike probability.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - the market has no framework for a whole-series revision and no consensus exists for the revised level
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: GBP/USD and EUR/GBP; the front end drives both

key_catalysts.event: ONS Consumer Price Inflation, July 2026, with producer prices
key_catalysts.rationale: The Bank of England projects headline CPI rising from 2.6% toward a 3.2% peak in Q4 2026 as energy passes through, with indirect energy effects adding roughly 0.5 percentage points in the second half. A print at or above 2.7% mechanically sustains the hawkish premium. Services CPI at 3.6% is the number the MPC actually watches, and services producer prices accelerated to 4.3% in Q2 from 3.2%.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - the rising path is expected, so only a sub-2.5% headline or a services print below 3.3% would move the front end

key_catalysts.event: S&P Global flash UK PMI (August) and ONS public sector finances (July)
key_catalysts.rationale: The confirmation test for the July composite jump to 52.1 from 49.3 and for the services rebound to 51.8 from 48.8. A second consecutive expansionary reading validates the growth turn that carries our tactical Bullish stance; a relapse below 50 removes it. The public finances release is the last major fiscal datapoint before the September Budget-representation deadline.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - flash PMI consensus for August was not available at the valuation date
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: GBP/USD and EUR/GBP; the PSF release matters for gilts and therefore for EUR/GBP

key_catalysts.event: Bank of England Decision Maker Panel survey (August round)
key_catalysts.rationale: The July round cut one-year CPI expectations to 3.4% from 3.7% and showed firms expecting their own wage growth to fall 0.6 percentage points to 3.4%. The MPC minutes cite DMP own-price expectations directly as a second-round-effects monitoring indicator, so a further decline is a direct input into the November Monetary Policy Report and a direct argument against the hike premium.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - the DMP is a specialist release the FX market rarely trades but the MPC reads closely
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/GBP; the front end drives the cross

key_catalysts.rationale: The formal close of external submissions to the 28 October Budget. Not market-moving in itself, but it marks the point after which Budget speculation and gilt-market positioning intensify, and historically the seven weeks between representation close and Budget day are when the fiscal risk premium builds into the long end.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not applicable - a procedural marker rather than a data event

key_catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council decision, Berlin, with updated staff projections
key_catalysts.rationale: Market-implied probability of a 25bp hike to a 2.50% deposit rate is 77-83%. Euro-area July flash HICP rose to 2.9% with core at 2.5%, both above the UK's 2.6% and 2.6%, so the euro area has the stronger inflation case. A hike compresses sterling's 150bp Bank Rate premium to 125bp in a single move and is the first leg of the strategic convergence trade.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Mostly - 77-83% of a 25bp move is priced, so the surprise is in the guidance for a second hike rather than the move itself
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/GBP is the direct expression; the sterling ERI has a 40% euro weight

key_catalysts.event: FOMC decision with Summary of Economic Projections; ONS Consumer Price Inflation, August 2026 (same day)
key_catalysts.rationale: The Fed held 9-3 on 29 July with Hammack, Kashkari and Logan dissenting for a HIKE, and core PCE at 3.29% year-on-year is 69bp above UK core CPI. A Fed hike inverts sterling's 12.5bp Cable carry advantage outright. The same day brings UK August CPI, so the Cable rate differential is repriced from both ends within hours.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially - a hold is the base case but the three hawkish dissents and the SEP make this the highest-variance Fed meeting of the window
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: GBP/USD directly; the simultaneous UK CPI makes this the single densest Cable event of the strategic window

key_catalysts.event: Bank of England MPC decision AND the annual quantitative-tightening review
key_catalysts.rationale: A double catalyst. The rate decision carries a 38% market-implied hike probability after a 6-3 vote in July; separately the Committee must set the next twelve-month QT envelope, having run GBP 70bn from October 2025 with the APF gilt stock at GBP 491bn on 17 July against a GBP 488bn end-September target. The Bank has already cut long-maturity auctions to zero in Q3, so a slower envelope would ease the 5.79% 30Y and is sterling-ambiguous, while maintaining the pace into a fragile long end is sterling-negative.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially on rates (38% hike); NOT priced on QT - no consensus for the envelope was retrievable
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: GBP/USD and EUR/GBP; the QT decision matters most for the 30Y gilt and therefore for the crisis correlation

key_catalysts.event: ONS Q2 2026 balance of payments and quarterly national accounts
key_catalysts.rationale: The first current-account reading that fully captures the Q2 energy shock, with NBP gas up 64.95% year-on-year and Brent having peaked at USD 117 on 29 April. The Q1 deficit narrowed to 1.9% of GDP ex precious metals only because the primary-income deficit collapsed from GBP 11.9bn to GBP 3.9bn while the trade deficit widened GBP 5.1bn - an unstable composition that has been revised heavily in prior quarters.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - the FX market did not react to the Q1 release and does not currently trade the UK external account
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/GBP and GBP/NOK; the terms-of-trade channel is cleanest against an energy exporter

key_catalysts.event: ONS Consumer Price Inflation, September 2026 - the Budget-relevant inflation print
key_catalysts.rationale: The last CPI release before the Budget and the one that sets the RPI reference for index-linked gilt uplift and for benefit and pension uprating decisions. With GBP 672.67bn of index-linked gilts in issue and RPI at 3.0%, a high print feeds directly into the debt-interest line the OBR must score on 28 October.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - the fiscal transmission from September CPI is a mechanism the FX market rarely trades in advance

key_catalysts.event: UK Budget (Chancellor John Healey's first) with the OBR autumn Economic and Fiscal Outlook
key_catalysts.rationale: The single highest-variance scheduled event for sterling in the next six months. It carries the cycle's ONLY formal assessment of the fiscal rules, because assessment moved to once a year. The anchor headroom figure of GBP 23.6bn against the stability rule was computed in March 2026, before the escalation that took Brent to USD 117, and the OBR itself said the conflict could have very significant impacts. A new government with a 10% probability of winning a majority has already announced four loosening measures in its first two weeks.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced at all - the volatility term structure is in contango with no visible Budget premium, and sterling's real effective rate sits 0.20% above its own mean
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: All sterling crosses; the cleanest expression is EUR/GBP and the tail expression is the 30Y gilt

key_catalysts.event: Bank of England MPC decision and November Monetary Policy Report
key_catalysts.rationale: The forcing event for the guidance gap. Eight days after the Budget, the Committee must publish new forecasts and either validate an 87.2% cumulative December hike probability or repeat the July MPR's central projection of CPI at 1.7% in 2028 Q1 - below target - on a conditioning curve that embeds roughly two hikes by Q3 2027. Repeating the below-target projection is a formal statement that pricing is too restrictive.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced - the market has discounted the Governor's 30 July pushback and the Bank's own Market Participants Survey median of no change
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/GBP and GBP/USD; this is where our 25bp front-end repricing thesis resolves

key_catalysts.event: Bank of England MPC decision - final 2026 meeting
key_catalysts.rationale: The meeting at which the market currently assigns an 87.2% cumulative probability that Bank Rate is above 3.75%. By this date the Budget, the November MPR, three further CPI prints and three labour market reports will all have landed, so this is the resolution point for the entire hawkish-premium debate. It also falls on the last sitting day before the Christmas recess, in thin year-end liquidity.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Fully priced as a hike-or-hold with an 87.2% cumulative hike probability and 0.1% cumulative cut probability

A move back above 4.0% would validate the second-round-effects thesis, push the December cumulative hike probability above 95% and make an actual hike the base case, which removes the front-end repricing that carries our strategic Bearish stance.

It would also validate the three dissenters against the Governor, which is a credibility shift in the hawkish direction.

It would simultaneously remove the hawkish premium, so the net effect on sterling is genuinely ambiguous rather than positive - which is why the resulting stance is Neutral rather than Bullish.

The squeeze mechanics of a crowded structural short unwinding into a fiscal-credibility improvement are the fastest sterling-positive path available.

Systematic trend capital would add on the break, and the structural thesis embedded in Factors 5 and 8 would have been rejected by the price.

A move above 4.0% - which the 18 August AWE seasonal-adjustment review could deliver mechanically through revision rather than through new data - would restore the wage-persistence case, validate the hawks and remove the basis for expecting a below-target November MPR projection.

change_since_last_report._narrative: The prior compatible dossier is GBP_Base_Currency_Dossier_2026-07-01 (framework v2.0). Note that the repository's Analysis/2026-07-01/Base folder is empty in this session's view, so the comparison is made against the engine-folder copy of that dossier, which is the same v2.0 artefact. The comparison below is of FINAL OUTPUTS ONLY - stances, confidence, conviction, weighted scores, rankings and signpost outcomes. No stance in this dossier was revised as a result of it.

factors_changed.reason: The hawkish rate story is now fully priced rather than emerging. On 1 July the market had not yet seen the 6-3 vote; by 31 July the OIS strip carried an 87.2% cumulative December hike probability with zero cuts across twelve months, and the Governor had publicly disowned the hike interpretation. With 87% already in the price there is almost no hawkish upside left and roughly 25-30bp of dovish repricing available, which converts a directional positive into a balanced factor.

Three relative legs that were open questions a month ago have resolved against sterling: the ECB is now 77-83% priced to hike on 10 September with euro-area core HICP at 2.5% above UK core at 2.6%, the Fed held 9-3 with three dissents to HIKE, and the July Monetary Policy Report published a central CPI projection of 1.7% in 2028 Q1 - below target - on a conditioning curve embedding roughly two hikes.

The wage and expectations channels all decelerated within the month: private-sector regular pay printed 2.9%, the softest since 2020; Decision Maker Panel one-year CPI expectations fell to 3.4% from 3.7%; Citi/YouGov household one-year expectations fell to 3.4% from 3.8%; and services CPI eased to 3.6% from 3.7%.

The risk backdrop improved measurably: the VIX ended July at 17.09, investment-grade credit held at an 80bp option-adjusted spread, MSCI World is up 9.42% year-to-date and the FTSE 100 up 9.43%. The stance change is a level change, not a re-rating of sterling's risk beta.

A complete inversion in the leveraged-fund cut. On 23 June leveraged funds were net long just 7,567 contracts after cutting 9,269 on the week; by 28 July they were net long 41,097 after four consecutive weekly builds totalling 152%, placing them at the 88th percentile of the sample. What was a clean, un-crowded long is now the most crowded fast-money position in the book.

Asset managers extended their short by 21,822 contracts in the week to 28 July, taking gross shorts to 153,344, or 57.3% of total open interest. A structural short of that concentration, added into a rising market, becomes squeeze fuel rather than a neutral observation.

factors_changed.factor: 5: External Balance & Terms of Trade - tactical
factors_changed.reason: UK NBP front-month gas rose 40.86% in a single month to 143.24 pence per therm and is now up 64.95% year-on-year, against a net energy import dependency that rose to 47.1%. The real three-month trade deficit widened GBP 3.3bn to minus GBP 17.5bn, faster than the nominal deficit - an import-price shock signature that was not present a month ago.

The 30 July communication was two-sided in a way the June meeting was not. The vote hardened from 7-2 to 6-3, which is hawkish, but the Governor's published opening remarks attribute the curve's upward slope to risk premia rather than rate expectations and disclose that the Bank's own Market Participants Survey median expects no change over the year ahead. The two offset.

The July Monetary Policy Report supplied the evidence that was missing on 1 July: a below-target CPI projection at the policy horizon on a tightening conditioning curve. In the Bank's own framework that is a formal statement that market pricing is too restrictive, and the 5 November MPR is the dated forcing event for it.

The US-Iran memorandum announced on 17 June collapsed from 8 July into strikes and retaliation, a Houthi Red Sea blockade was imposed around 24 July and QatarEnergy extended LNG force majeure to European and Asian customers to at least end-September. The energy tail moved from dormant to active inside the month.

The most consequential single re-rating in the dossier. The prior report read dollar funding as a headwind with the DXY at a fifteen-month high near 101; a month later the DXY is 99.914, SOFR prints exactly level with interest on reserve balances at 3.65%, Standing Repo Facility usage is zero, overnight reverse repo is drained to USD 2.151bn, and the Federal Reserve executed roughly USD 30.4bn of reserve-management Treasury bill purchases in July with total assets USD 202.4bn above their December 2025 trough.

Same mechanism at a longer lag: a central bank that has switched from shrinking to growing its balance sheet supplies a persistent, not a one-off, liquidity impulse, and it runs through the entire strategic window.

signposts_triggered.signpost: BoE Bank Rate and MPC vote split (prior level: 3.75%, 7-2 hold with two dissents for a hike)
signposts_triggered.outcome: TRIGGERED HAWKISH. The 30 July vote was 6-3, with Greene, Mann and Pill all voting to raise Bank Rate to 4.00% - the dissent count rose from two to three and the market moved the December cumulative hike probability to 87.2%.
signposts_triggered.implication: This is the signpost that most clearly moved AGAINST our strategic bearish thesis, and we have honoured it by holding tactical Factor 1 at Neutral rather than turning it Bearish. It does not change the strategic view because the Governor and both Deputy Governors publicly disowned the hawkish reading on the same day.

signposts_triggered.outcome: CONFIRMED. The June print eased to 3.6%, and is now 0.9 percentage points below the 4.5% March peak.
signposts_triggered.implication: The MPC's key underlying gauge continues to decelerate, which supports the strategic Bearish stances on Factors 2 and 6 and is the direct evidence behind our expectation of a below-target November MPR projection.

signposts_triggered.outcome: PARTIALLY TRIGGERED. The spread narrowed 8bp to plus 183bp, but only because BOTH legs rose sharply - the gilt to 5.038% and the Bund to 3.2036%. The spread remains the widest since the September 2022 mini-budget.

new_catalysts: 28 October 2026 - the UK Budget, confirmed only on 31 July 2026 and therefore absent from the prior report. It is Chancellor John Healey's first Budget and carries the cycle's only formal fiscal-rules assessment.

20 July 2026 - the change of Prime Minister and Chancellor. Andy Burnham replaced Keir Starmer and John Healey replaced Rachel Reeves; the prior report was written under the previous administration and could not have anticipated it.
17 September 2026 - the MPC decision now doubles as the annual quantitative-tightening review, making it a dual catalyst the prior report treated as a rate decision only.
18 August 2026 - the ONS average-weekly-earnings seasonal-adjustment review, which ONS has stated may revise the entire historical wage series and which lands in the labour market publication.
10 September 2026 - the ECB Governing Council meeting in Berlin, now carrying a 77-83% market-implied hike probability that did not exist a month ago.
End-September 2026 - the extended QatarEnergy LNG force majeure on European and Asian customers, which sets a hard date on the current gas-price regime.

5 November 2026 - the November Monetary Policy Report, elevated from a routine event to the forcing point for the guidance gap because the July MPR published a below-target medium-term CPI projection.

seasonality.pattern: Two documented sterling patterns fall inside the horizons. The first is thin August liquidity: UK institutional participation drops sharply from the first week of August, and with the Commons in recess until 1 September and the MPC not meeting until 17 September, Cable's realised volatility historically compresses through mid-August before the release cluster. The second is the year-end portfolio rebalancing and January effect that affects all G10 currencies, which falls at the far end of the strategic window. The UK's own documented April fiscal year-end hedging pattern is NOT in the window and is not applied here.
seasonality.relevance_window: August 2026 for the thin-liquidity effect - specifically the 3-12 August period before the 13 August data cluster - and December 2026 to January 2027 for year-end rebalancing, which sits at the end of the strategic horizon and coincides with the 17 December MPC decision on the last sitting day before the Christmas recess.
seasonality.historical_magnitude: The thin-August effect is a volatility rather than a direction effect and typically compresses realised volatility by one to two points before the autumn release calendar restores it; Cable's twenty-day realised at 6.41% sits at the 65th percentile of its trailing year, so it is entering August ABOVE its usual seasonal position. Year-end rebalancing magnitude is not separately quantifiable for sterling from the sources available this cycle and is noted qualitatively rather than sized.
seasonality.current_alignment: Partially aligned and partially contradicted. The thin-liquidity pattern supports our expectation of a grind rather than a trend through the first half of August, and it amplifies the risk that a break of the 1.3400 moving-average convergence produces an outsized move. It is contradicted by the fact that realised volatility is already running above its seasonal norm at the 65th percentile, and by an unusually dense 13-21 August release calendar that will override any seasonal quiet.

assumptions: Spot and cross rates are taken from the cycle data snapshot at the 31 July 2026 close, with GBP/USD at 1.34834. Weekend fills were stripped from the cached daily series before computing moving averages, realised volatility and period performance, because the vendor series carries non-trading-day rows that would otherwise bias every calculation. Where the cycle cache holds a precise current number - spot FX, US rates and yields, CFTC positioning, BIS real effective exchange rates, commodity prices, OECD macro aggregates - the cache is treated as the source of truth and web research supplies context and citations around it. The CFTC percentile rankings are computed over a 26-week window because the cached Commitments of Traders series begins on 3 February 2026. They cannot support the multi-year percentiles the framework contemplates and are labelled as short-window rankings throughout. The BIS real effective exchange rate percentile of 53 is computed over 30 monthly observations because the cached series begins in January 2024. The PPP deviation table is constructed as the relative deviation of each currency's real effective rate from its own 30-month mean, which is a real-effective relative-value method rather than an absolute purchasing-power-parity calculation, and it is applied identically across all eleven currencies in this cycle for consistency.
